name: The JED Foundation
description: Emotional health and suicide prevention resources for teens and young adults. Programs for schools and communities.

sections.title: About The JED Foundation
sections.text: The JED Foundation (JED) is a nonprofit organization that partners with teens, young adults, families, high schools, and colleges to strengthen mental health and prevent suicide. Founded in 2000 by Donna and Phil Satow after losing their son Jed to suicide, the organization has become a leading voice in adolescent and young adult mental health. JED works to build emotional resilience and help young people thrive, equipping them with skills and support before crisis occurs.

sections.title: Resources for Teens and Young Adults
sections.text: JED offers extensive free resources for teens and young adults through Set to Go, a comprehensive guide for managing the transition from high school to college or adult life. The website provides practical advice on handling stress, relationships, substance use, and mental health challenges. JED's content addresses common concerns like anxiety, depression, identity exploration, and academic pressure. Resources include videos, articles, self-care tools, and guidance on when and how to seek professional help.

sections.title: JED Campus Program
sections.text: JED Campus is a four-year program that partners with colleges and universities to evaluate and strengthen their mental health, substance misuse, and suicide prevention efforts. Schools work with JED experts to assess current programs, develop strategic plans, and implement evidence-based practices. Over 400 colleges have enrolled in JED Campus, creating safer and more supportive environments for millions of students. The program addresses seven key areas including developing life skills, promoting social connectedness, and following crisis management procedures.

sections.title: High School Programs
sections.text: JED High School extends the organization's expertise to secondary education, helping schools build comprehensive mental health strategies. The program provides assessment tools, resources, and technical assistance to help schools promote emotional well-being, identify students at risk, and respond effectively to mental health crises. JED partners with school administrators, counselors, teachers, and student leaders to create school cultures where mental health is prioritized and students feel comfortable seeking help.

sections.title: Resources for Parents and Families
sections.text: JED provides resources for parents and families to help them support the mental health of young people. Guides cover topics like recognizing warning signs, having conversations about mental health, understanding treatment options, and supporting a young person in crisis. JED's Parent Guide helps families prepare for the emotional challenges of major life transitions. The organization also offers resources specifically for parents who have lost a child to suicide, connecting them with support communities and healing resources.
